title: Mexican Quiche
description:
This recipe is a family favorite from Grandma Lamort. We often refer to it as a Mexican crustless quiche. It is an easy and fun dish to serve for breakfast, brunch or lunch and is a standard at our tailgates. We usually serve the casserole at room temperature, but it can also be served warm right out of the oven.
The original recipe called for a 7 ounce can of chopped green chilies and ½ pint fresh tomatoes chopped. With the increasing availability of delicious varieties of fresh salsa (you can choose mild, medium or hot, according to your preference), we have found that substituting drained salsa for the chilies and tomatoes adds a special perkiness to the dish.
START TO FINISH: 60 MIN
Grandma’s Mexican Casserole
Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
In a large mixing bowl, blend eggs, cottage cheese, baking powder, salt and flour.
Drain salsa so that most of the liquid is removed.
Add shredded cheese and drained salsa to the egg/cheese mixture. Blend thoroughly.
Pour the mixture into a buttered 9” x 13” baking pan (metal or glass is fine).
Bake casserole for 15 minutes at 400 degrees; reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees and bake an additional 30 minutes or until the top of the casserole is a beautiful golden brown.
For serving, cut the casserole into 24 pieces.
